newsitem.title: UK: Slow EU grains market unchanged to easier.
newsitem.headline: Slow EU grains market unchanged to easier.

text.p: European domestic grain prices were unchanged to easier this week as much of the trade appeared to settle early into a Christmas lull, traders said.
French wheat prices were worst hit by fading hopes of a pickup in export business amid competition from Argentina and Australia.
News Egypt bought Argentine and Australian wheat on Sunday will mean more pressure on the European Commission to hike export refunds, they said.
French maize prices were steady. "Demand is thin and sellers are in no hurry to sell," one dealer said.
There have been no new export sales of German wheat this week, brokers said.
"It's very quiet but prices are holding because of Eastern European export hopes for early 1997...there are already some enquiries," one said.
Domestic markets saw some trader buying from farmers and cooperatives, but many operators started to wind down operations ahead of the Christmas and New Year holidays.
"Exports to third countries and European millers have not been too successful to date and this means volume pressure, which keeps a lid on prices," another broker said.
But opportunities were seen to compete with U.S. wheat because of the firm dollar, and Spain and Britain were expected to seek German top quality wheat for blending.
Barley was sluggish as Danish and northern German feed manufacturers made only sporadic purchases and export markets failed to offer outlets for German supplies.

Brokers said feedgrain markets should be underpinned by additional demand arising from the price stability of competing imported feeds. Feed wheat from other EU origins was likely to compete with German barley and wheat.
Spanish dealers said the market had been particularly dull with buyers entering the market on a very limited basis.
This was reflected in a slight softening in ex-farm prices across the board in the week to December 11.
Feed wheat prices eased marginally with buyers continuing to opt for cheaper feed grains.
Barley prices held steady although traders said they expected to see some weakening as farmers had not sold what they had expected to after a plentiful harvest.
"There's still a lot of barley around and the next harvest is only five to six months away," said one trader.
Traders said the European Commission debate on U.S. gene-modified maize had silenced the maize market.
A decision to allow countries to import modified U.S. maize would put pressure on prices and buyers were reluctant to enter the market before they knew the outcome.
Traders said they expected business to pick up in the new year, after the EU decision.

Italian durum wheat prices rose slightly as internal demand picked up ahead of Christmas holidays and as some industrial buyers started to arrange supplies for January. Dealers also noted foreign durum wheat prices rose making domestic durum wheat more attractive.
Soft wheat prices were largely unchanged this week, while maize prices fell somewhat this week.
The UK market has spent the past week dominated by currency moves rather than fundamental market news, traders said. Consumer interest has been limited, they said.

Prices for fob feed barley are 2 stg higher than for feed wheat. Traders blamed shipper interest as exporters move to cover business to Saudi Arabia. There are other export destinations for barley, but the Saudi business dominates in volume terms, they said.
In the short term a lack of farmer selling is supporting the market, traders said. But in the longer term they expected oversupply to reassert itself and inject a more bearish tone.
